newsitem.title: INDIA: India call, gilts end steady, look to repo results.
newsitem.headline: India call, gilts end steady, look to repo results.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday at 8.75-9.0 percent, slightly down from opening quotes of 9.25-9.75 percent and dealers said a repo auction, to be held later in the day, will decide the level of call money rates for Saturday.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) holds a four-day repo auction of government securities later in the day.
Dealers said the level of participation in the repo auction will determine call money rates on Saturday.
"It all depends how much money flows out at the repo auction," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "If there is a big outflow, call money may not come down from current levels."
High subscriptions at the repo will neutralise the effects of an RBI repurchase of securities on Saturday.
The RBI repurchases 51.5 billion rupees of securities on Saturday.
"Earlier, there was a feeling that this money will come back to the market and call money will come down," said a dealer at a state-run bank.

"But now some market players feel big lenders may choose to put money in the repo auction in a bid to keep funds supply in call monmey market tight," he said. "In that case, call money will remain high and security prices may also see a correction."
Dealers said prices of government securities were largely steady in brisk trade.

"Prices were stable to slightly higher for most stocks," said another dealer. "Stocks with three to five year maturities went up by around 0.2 rupees...it all depends now on how call behaves tomorrow."
The 13.50 percent 1998 governemnt stock traded at 103.32 rupees, the 12 percent 1999 at 102.55, the 12.50 percent 2004 at 100.25 and the 12.59 percent 2004 at 100.4, dealers said.
